$comment: OUTBOUND LINKS THAT MUST BE PRESENT AND MUST RESOLVE.
Why this exists, dated 2026-08-16: /agentic-terminal carried a primary CTA,
It returned 404. The page's only call to action for the tier it was advertising
was dead, and nothing in this repository looked at an outbound link, so nothing
could notice. Every other claim surface here fails the build when it drifts.
TWO HALVES, and the second is the one that gets skipped.
presence  a declared URL missing from its page FAILS. A CTA can be broken by
deletion as easily as by a 404, and deletion is the quieter failure.
status    a declared URL that does not resolve FAILS.
Undeclared outbound links are swept too, and a 404 or 410 on any of them fails.
That sweep is deliberately narrower: a transport error or a 5xx on somebody
else's host is reported as NOT CHECKED rather than failing our build, because a
third party's outage is not our defect. A 404 is different. It means the address
we published does not name anything, which is a fact about our page.
This file is for links we ASSERT. It is not an allowlist and adding a row does
not make a link exempt from anything.

mustResolve.why: The design-partner CTA and the page's own citation of the status section it is reconciled against. If this stops resolving, the page is asserting a reconciliation against a document nobody can reach.
The open-source claim on this page is checkable only by following it. A dead link here turns 'free, open source, self-hostable' into an assertion.

$skipHostsNote: Font CDNs only. They are referenced from every page, they are not claims, and checking them 38 times per run buys nothing. Anything that carries a claim stays in the sweep.
